title: bug: get_commit_scope keeps excluding a dependent's planned paths after this task is DONE, so a QA exit landing sweeps the dependent's mid-step edits
description:
governor-4764040b measured this at 18:21Z (#governors msg-5fcf216b). governor-693b7073 verified it on HEAD.

What happened:
- WT-08 (task-7a4aab5e) became DONE at 18:15:01Z. fa7fece5 (dependsOn WT-08) was claimed at once, and its step 1 (affectedFiles [scripts/moe-agent.sh]) ran IN_PROGRESS from 18:15:27Z to 18:17:43Z.
- WT-08's QA session exited at 18:16:21Z. Its landing, wip baa704f5 `[status=DONE role=qa]`, committed and pushed fa7fece5's half-done scripts/moe-agent.sh edit (the bash 3.2 heredoc→function refactor, +44/-19) under WT-08's task id.
- The QA session's pre-flight (17:41:28Z) had seen the file clean, so the wrapper's "changed since my pre-flight" rule took the bytes as its own.

Cause: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.ts:160-168.
- `waitsOnThis = findDependencyPath(state, other.id, task.id) !== null` makes a dependent contribute only its ASSERTED paths. The comment reads "cannot have run yet: dependsOn gates its WORKING claims until this task is DONE".
- The code never checks whether THIS task is already DONE/ARCHIVED, or whether the dependent is active.
- Once this task is terminal, its dependents are claimable and editing. Their planned and IN_PROGRESS step paths then enter neither the peer set nor editingTaskIds, so nothing is held.

Impact:
- Every serialized-lane handoff (wrapper lane, any dependsOn chain) can put the next row's mid-step bytes into the previous row's QA exit commit.
- Attribution is wrong: the dependent's completion commit lacks those paths.
- Worse, unreviewed mid-step wrapper bytes reach HEAD, and seats hot-reload committed moe-agent.* bytes.

Fix shape:
- Apply the waitsOnThis exclusion only while THIS task is non-terminal AND the waiting peer has no active assignee and no open attempt.
- Otherwise the dependent is an ordinary peer: its planned and IN_PROGRESS paths count, with peerActive/editingTaskIds as for any peer.
- Keep the original intent: a serialized chain's not-yet-started links must not contest the link before them.
- Update the tool description string and docs/MCP_SERVER.md's get_commit_scope PEER text to match.

Note: the running daemon gets this fix only after a rebuild and restart. That is human-coordinated, using the staging-build swap; never build in place in the shared checkout.
definitionOfDone: With this task DONE (or ARCHIVED), a dependent's planned and IN_PROGRESS step paths appear in peerDeclared (and in editingTaskIds while it is active), so a later exit landing of this task holds them instead of committing them.

While this task is non-terminal, a dependent with no active assignee and no open attempt still contributes only its ASSERTED paths: a serialized chain's unstarted links do not contest the link before them, as today.

getCommitScope.test.ts has regression tests for: a terminal task with an active, editing dependent (held); a non-terminal task with an idle dependent (asserted only); and a non-terminal task with an active dependent (counted).
The get_commit_scope tool description and docs/MCP_SERVER.md describe the new rule.
The daemon vitest suite for getCommitScope, plus the full daemon suite, passes in a snapshot (never an in-place build in the shared checkout), and its output is supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.description:
The fix. Edit only packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.ts.
(a) Add this helper next to peerTaskActive: `function dependentMayRun(state: StateManager, other: Task, nowMs: number, sinceMs: number | null): boolean { const assignee = other.assignedWorkerId ? state.getWorker(other.assignedWorkerId) : null; if (assignee && isPeerActive(assignee, nowMs, sinceMs)) return true; return listAttempts(state, other.id).some((attempt) => attempt.phase !== 'closed'); }`. Its JSDoc must say why it is deliberately narrower than peerTaskActive:
  - It has no fail-closed shortcut when since is missing, and no clause for a recent phase change. An idle link has not started, even one whose planning attempt closed inside the window, or any link when since is missing. Counting it would reopen task-435683c2: a serialized chain's unstarted link contesting the link before it.
  - A session that can write bytes always holds a non-closed attempt: claimNextTask's openClaimAttempt opens one per claim, and taskStore's closeAttemptsOnHandBack closes it when the seat is cleared. running, reconciling and finalizing all count as open.
(b) Just before the peer loop, add `const thisTerminal = TERMINAL_STATUSES.has(task.status);`. Use the raw status on purpose; see the risks note.
(c) Replace `const waitsOnThis = findDependencyPath(state, other.id, task.id) !== null;` with `const waitsOnThis = !thisTerminal && !dependentMayRun(state, other, nowMs, sinceMs) && findDependencyPath(state, other.id, task.id) !== null;`. The explicit terminal check is required: findDependencyPath (state/dependencyUnblock.ts) matches a DONE/ARCHIVED target before its status skip, which is the root cause.
(d) Rewrite the comment above that line. The exclusion applies only while this task is not DONE/ARCHIVED and the waiting peer has no active assignee and no open attempt. Once this task is terminal, its dependents are claimable and may be mid-step: in baa704f5, WT-08's QA exit landing committed fa7fece5's half-done scripts/moe-agent.sh under WT-08's id. A dependent with a live session is an ordinary peer, whatever the edges say.
(e) In the tool description's PEER clause, replace 'a peer that waits on this task contributes only its asserted paths, since it cannot have run yet;' with 'while this task is not DONE/ARCHIVED, a peer that waits on it (dependsOn or blockedOnTaskIds, transitively) and has no active assignee and no open attempt contributes only its asserted paths, since it cannot have run yet; once this task is DONE/ARCHIVED, or while that peer has an active assignee or an open attempt, it counts like any other peer;'.
Error handling: add no new throw path. One peer's junk record must never fail another task's scope. dependentMayRun uses the same getWorker and listAttempts calls that peerTaskActive already survives: a non-string or unknown assignedWorkerId resolves to no assignee, and an unrecognised attempt phase counts as open, so it fails closed and the peer is counted. The handler's existing input validation (missing taskId, bad phase, unparsable since, unknown task) is unchanged.
Change nothing else. These stay as they are: the peerPaths, active and editing lines; peerTaskActive; inProgressStepPaths; TERMINAL_STATUSES; the reply shape (no new field); and both wrappers. A counted dependent then gets peerActive, activeTaskIds and editingTaskIds by the same rule as any peer. Keep this invariant: for every board state, the new peerDeclared is a superset of the old one. Paths and contributors are only added, and peerActive only flips false to true, so the fix only adds holds and never releases one. After this step, every step-1 test passes.
implementationPlan.note: Fix in getCommitScope.ts: new helper dependentMayRun (assignee active via isPeerActive, or any non-closed attempt; no since fail-closed shortcut, no recent-phase clause), const thisTerminal before the peer loop, waitsOnThis = !thisTerminal && !dependentMayRun(...) && findDependencyPath(...) !== null, rewritten comment, tool-description PEER clause updated. One deviation from the plan's helper body, to honour the contract line 'malformed assignee data fails closed': a non-string assignedWorkerId returns true (like isAssigneeProtected), because getWorker(42) just returns null and the peer would otherwise be excluded. Missing/DEAD/stale owners stay uncounted (T-B pins that). Added test T-D (numeric assignee + garbage attempt phase are counted, no throw) to the new describe, so the narrow file is 65 tests, not 64. Snapshot run: getCommitScope.test.ts 65 passed (65); tsc --noEmit clean.

implementationPlan.description:
Docs. Edit only docs/MCP_SERVER.md, the '### moe.get_commit_scope' Returns block.
Replace the peerDeclared comment text 'except a peer that waits on this task (dependsOn ∪ blockedOnTaskIds, transitively) contributes its asserted paths only: dependsOn gates it from WORKING until this task is DONE, so its plan is intent, not an edit.' with the new rule, keeping the aligned `//` comment column:
  - While this task is not DONE/ARCHIVED, a peer that waits on it (dependsOn ∪ blockedOnTaskIds, transitively) and has no active assignee (peerActive's assignee test) and no non-closed attempt contributes its asserted paths only. dependsOn gates it from WORKING until this task is DONE, so its plan is intent, not an edit.
  - Once this task is DONE/ARCHIVED, its dependents are claimable. A waiting peer with an active assignee or an open attempt may be mid-step. Either one counts like any other peer: planned and IN_PROGRESS paths, peerActive, activeTaskIds and editingTaskIds.
Also change '...so a waits-on-this peer still contributes its asserted paths only.' to '...so an excluded waits-on-this peer still contributes its asserted paths only.'
No other doc states the rule: a grep for 'waits on this' over docs/ and every CLAUDE.md found only these lines. Do not touch any other section. Four open tasks plan or assert edits elsewhere in this file (WT-17, CQ-V12 and CQ-M06 PENDING; CQ-R13 BLOCKED, asserted). Use the Edit tool only: a TOOL witness is what lets this contested path land.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe.get_commit_scope drops the non-asserted paths of a peer that waits on the scoped task (dependsOn ∪ blockedOnTaskIds, transitively) only while two things hold: the scoped task is not DONE/ARCHIVED, and the peer has no active assignee (isPeerActive) and no non-closed attempt. In every other case the waiting peer is an ordinary PEER contributor: its planned and IN_PROGRESS step paths count, and its peerActive, activeTaskIds and editingTaskIds are computed exactly as for any peer.
invariants: For every board state, the new peerDeclared is a superset of the old one. Paths and contributors are only added, and peerActive only flips false to true, so the change only adds landing holds and never releases one.

While the scoped task is non-terminal, a dependent that is unassigned or whose owner is DEAD, missing or stale, and that has no open attempt, contributes only its asserted paths. This holds with or without since, including when its planning attempt closed inside the window.
The reply shape is unchanged: no new field. The tool stays read-only apart from the existing liveness touch.
Error handling: one peer's junk record never fails another task's scope. No new throw path; malformed assignee or attempt data fails closed, so the peer is counted.
compatibility: scripts/moe-agent.sh, scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and their disk fallback are unchanged; they already treat PEER entries as holds.
The existing serialized-chain tests in getCommitScope.test.ts (~:203, ~:240) pass unchanged.
approvedScope: getCommitScope.ts: new module helper dependentMayRun; the waitsOnThis expression and its comment in the handler's peer loop; the PEER clause of the tool description
getCommitScope.test.ts: the inverted ~:745 test and a new describe('waits-on-this exclusion (task-44a07f00)')
docs/MCP_SERVER.md: the get_commit_scope Returns block's peerDeclared comment lines
sourceAssumptions: packages/moe-daemon/src/state/dependencyUnblock.ts findDependencyPath matches a DONE/ARCHIVED target before its status skip.
packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.ts peerTaskActive returns true without since and counts an attempt phase change inside the window.

packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts openClaimAttempt opens an attempt per claim; packages/moe-daemon/src/state/taskStore.ts closeAttemptsOnHandBack closes non-finalizing attempts when the seat is cleared.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) Reuse peerTaskActive as the 'dependent is active' test. Rejected for two reasons. It fails closed when since is missing: every dependent then counts, which brings back the task-435683c2 serialized-chain regression for callers that omit since and fails the existing ~:203 test. And its recent-phase-change clause counts a link whose planning attempt closed during this task's review, which is the normal serialized-lane case.
(2) Gate on the dependent's own unmet dependencies (isDependencySatisfied or unmetDependsOn) instead of this task's raw terminal status. This is more precise under a strict deliveryPolicy and for transitive chains. But the DoD names DONE/ARCHIVED, and the running check already covers real activity. Counting an idle dependent that is still gated only adds holds; with since its peerActive is false, so the idle-clean exception still lands paths that were clean at pre-flight.
(3) A presence-free assignee test: any registered non-DEAD owner, as assigneeProtected uses. Rejected to keep the tool's existing 'active assignee' meaning (isPeerActive). Any session that can write bytes holds a non-closed attempt, and the attempt arm catches that whatever the presence.
(4) A wrapper-side fix. Rejected: dependency knowledge lives in the daemon. Once the peer map is right, the wrapper's existing MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_EDITING hold does the right thing, with no sh/ps1 parity churn. The wrapper's disk fallback already counts every open task in full (fail closed) and needs no change.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Root cause. findDependencyPath (state/dependencyUnblock.ts:174) checks `id === targetId` before it skips DONE/ARCHIVED nodes. So it returns a path when the TARGET is DONE, and waitsOnThis stayed true after this task finished.
Wrapper consumption (scripts/moe-agent.sh resolve_attribution, ~:4255-4300). PEER membership only ever adds skips: MOE_ATTR_PEER_DECLARED, CONTESTED_EDITING and CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED. With editingTaskIds naming the dependent, the incident path lands as MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_EDITING(task-fa7fece5) instead of committing through own_bytes.
Attempts. Every claim opens one (claimNextTask openClaimAttempt). A hand-back closes the non-finalizing ones (taskStore closeAttemptsOnHandBack). So an idle WORKING row waiting on the gate has no open attempt.
Architect prototype, on a scratch archive of d40c2847:
  - Before the fix, exactly (1), T-A and T-C fail and T-B passes.
  - After it, getCommitScope.test.ts passes 64/64, and the full daemon suite passes: 218 files, 6434 passed / 20 skipped (HEAD alone: 6431 / 20).
  - Mutants M1-M6 are all killed by real assertion failures.
The prototype is reference only and may be cleaned: /tmp/claude-1000/-mnt-d-projexts-moes/1b65d15e-a468-4704-b5a3-19fabfe7d4b3/scratchpad/gate44/repo/packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.ts and getCommitScope.test.ts. Never cp it into the checkout: write with the Edit tool (global rail: shell writes leave no TOOL witness).
planningNotes.risks:
Intended behavior change. A terminal task's later exit landing, usually QA's, now holds paths that a dependent's plan names instead of sweeping them: EDITING while the dependent is mid-step, UNTOUCHED when the path was dirty at pre-flight.
A dependent of a non-terminal task with a live session now contests too. Examples: an edge added after its claim, a kept-seat block, an architect re-planning a reopened row that still has its old plan. This is fail closed, and rare.
Raw DONE counts as terminal even under a strict deliveryPolicy, so an idle dependent still gated on evidence is counted. That only adds holds.
Test pitfalls:
  - openAttempt must run after h.state.load().
  - T-A's entry order is task-id order, then each task's asserted-then-planned order.
  - vitest colours its output; use NO_COLOR=1, and grep -a, because a log can contain NUL bytes.
  - Restore mutants from the checkout copy and cmp before citing the gate.
The running daemon gets the fix only after a human-coordinated staging-build swap and a restart. Never build in place.
Other tasks touch docs/MCP_SERVER.md: WT-17, CQ-V12 and CQ-M06 have it in PENDING plan steps, and BLOCKED CQ-R13 asserts it. Edit only the get_commit_scope Returns lines, with the Edit tool, or the landing holds the file as CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED.
